title: edge of space
text: Edge of Space game team presents nicely polished product. Proven concept of Terraria taken to space works very nicely. Constant flow of updates ensures new content as well as bug fixes and patches that are already polishing the game despite its early access. Content is already rich in current build, more biomes are coming and planned. I personally hope for linux support which is currently not planned but there is only minor thing as it was not promised in the first place. Sound part is nothing to be ashamed of. Catchy song in main menu proves this 100%. Graphic is nice and art fits the theme very well. Interesting design of enemies should be mentioned. Where else are you going to meet bear with rocket launcher on its back or legions of crabs swarming you all directions. Early access is a big thing recently and it's up to us, gamers, to drive it in the right direction by supporting the developers who deserve it and excluding those who don't. Very responsive community management of EoS to all concerns shows how developer-community relationship should look like. This is certainly one of the best parts of the experience. Handyman Studios shows how early access should be done. By very active approach they are building nice community and nice reputation.

title: edge of space
text: I simply cannot recommend the game in this state. I was trying to wait out for updates, I was trying to wait for the developers to come back from their "logistics stuff" that they've been doing for months (it doesn't take that long for someone or even multiple people to move), and the developers have seemingly fallen off the face of the planet (maybe into the Edge of Space!? lol, couldn't resist, sorry). Starbound did a similar thing where Chucklefish relocated their entire company, but yet here's the thing: Chucklefish at least continued to maintain their website, and actually continued communications with the playerbase. Since Handyman Studios posted that update in April (It is October as I write this), there hasn't been any communication whatsoever, except for 1 tweet that advertised the game being on sale somewhere. So, since this appears to be abandonware, I believe I can attach my own review of this game. Do I recommend it as it is now? NO. Do I think it could be a good game? YES, but only if the developers actually come back. Do I hope they would come back and make it better? YES! The game has a nice premise going for it, but there are simply too many things wrong with it to make it an actual good purchase. If you really want a tech demo to mess around with, maybe for inspiration or ideas, go ahead. I'd wait until it's on sale, though. So, Pros/Cons: Pros: -A nice recipe unlock system -Good graphics for a sidescrolling indie game -Lots of inventive ideas (pets, character upgrades, etc) -A unique take on the sandbox exploration game (you progress by going down) -You start with a jetpack Cons: -Control/UI Bugs (your character will shoot their weapon or use their tool while dragging items around in the UI) -Unfinished game and obvious missing content (the last two biomes are not finished, some tech unlocks are empty) -Blah combat (you always feel weak as bleeep because your guns all suck, and it takes 10+ shots to kill anything) -Melee combat is useless -Cheap enemies that can fly through solid walls to attack you -Dungeons are buggy, some of those bugs were fixed in the last update, but some remain from what I've been told -No Real Map System (this is the huge deal-breaker for me -- you only have a "current" minimap of what you can currently see and that's it) -Somewhat clunky UI system (inventory management, everything freshly obtained gets dumped into the hotbar etc) -UI LAG. Yes, the UI lags when trying to move items around. Recap: A game that has/had a lot of potential but sadly fell way short. I tried hard to like this game, because when I first started playing it, I was like "I hope they finish this game or make it better!" But sadly.. it doesn't look like that will ever come to pass. If you're a game developer and you're looking for some inspiration, I'd suggest picking this game up on sale, maybe someone else can develop something else that is similar but way better?

Mine stuff, build armor and weapons, fight monsters, build a base. But it isn't quite the same. Definitely a game to watch if you liked terraria and don't like playing unfinished games.
